Day 1. Manoj pinned a large calendar to the wall above his desk and hung a red marker on a string. After his first walk-and-jog, he drew a cross on the date. It felt silly and satisfying at once.

Day 8. Harish, his flatmate, pointed at the gap on Sunday. "You missed one." "That's not a miss, that's a rest day," said Manoj, and drew a small green circle. He'd planned it, and his legs were grateful.

Day 21. Fifteen crosses in a row. Manoj noticed he had begun to feel anxious about breaking the chain, and once nearly went out with a sore throat. He wrote on the calendar, in small letters: Streak helps me. It does not own me.

qa.q: What colour marker hung on a string by the calendar?
What was Manoj feeling on Day 21 when he wrote the note in small letters?
qa.a: Manoj felt some anxiety about breaking the chain but also a wish to keep the habit healthy, so he reminded himself the streak was a helper.

qa.q: What could Manoj do if the streak begins to cause stress again, and why?
qa.a: Manoj could count rest days as part of the streak and allow a break when unwell, because a habit is only useful if it does not cause harm.

qa.q: How does Harish see the calendar and the Sunday gap?
qa.a: Harish sees a flatmate proud of the streak; pointing at the gap may be teasing, but the answer shows the rest was planned.

grounding: The person marks a wall calendar after each session and treats a rest day as planned recovery, while an obsessed streak can backfire.

passage:
"Madhav, you asked how your Dilnaz Khala got so disciplined. Truly, it was a calendar.
I was twenty-one, working at the bank, and I'd started and stopped exercising maybe ten times. Then my roommate gave me a big paper calendar from a sweet shop. I pinned it by the door.
Every evening I did my yoga or a walk, I made a fat red cross. Rest days, Wednesday and Sunday, got a green circle. Not a gap. A planned day off.
After three weeks the red crosses made a line, and I didn't want to break it. It pulled me off the sofa many times.
But I'll be honest. Once, with a fever, I did yoga anyway just to keep the line. I felt worse for days. After that I added a rule: a sick day is a green circle too.
So yes, mark the streak. Just don't let the streak mark you."

qa.q: What did Dilnaz Khala draw on rest days?
qa.a: She drew a green circle on rest days.

qa.q: How did Dilnaz feel when she saw the line of red crosses?
qa.a: She felt motivated and proud, not wanting to break the line, and it pulled her off the sofa many times.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and what did it teach?
qa.a: Doing yoga with a fever just to keep the line and feeling worse was the turning point; it led her to count sick days as planned rest too.

qa.q: How might the roommate who gave the calendar have seen the change?
qa.a: The roommate probably felt pleased and surprised to see a simple sweet-shop calendar turn into a steady habit.

grounding: Shows the person marking a calendar after each session and treating rest days as planned recovery, with a warning that obsessing over the streak can backfire.

Hemant's hostel room had no wall space, only a cupboard door covered in old stickers. The college gym opened at six and closed at eight, and his practical exams started in two weeks. He had failed to keep a routine twice.
This time he stuck a printed month on the cupboard door. After each session, even the short ones squeezed in before labs, he drew a tick. Tuesdays and Fridays had a pre-printed "R" for rest.
His roommate Vaibhav noticed the ticks growing. "Nineteen days," he said one night.
During exam week the gym closed early for maintenance, and Hemant felt his chest tighten looking at the empty square. He almost ran laps in the corridor at midnight just to earn a tick. Then he looked at the "R" squares and drew one more by hand, in pencil. "Planned rest," he muttered.
The next morning he was back at six.

qa.q: How many days of ticks did Vaibhav count?
How did Hemant feel when he looked at the empty square during exam week?
qa.a: He felt anxious, his chest tightening, and was tempted to run laps at midnight just to earn a tick.

qa.q: What else could Hemant do to keep the streak helpful rather than stressful?
qa.a: He could plan in advance for exam weeks and closures, marking them as rest or short home sessions, so a gap doesn't cause panic.

qa.q: How might Vaibhav see Hemant's calendar?
qa.a: Vaibhav notices the ticks growing and seems impressed, and might feel encouraged to try something similar.

grounding: Shows the person marking a visible calendar after each session and treating rest days as planned recovery, and resisting obsessing over the streak.
